source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 10, Schedule 1 Line 48b; PDF page 24, Pension and Annuity Worksheet (Line 2 takes all of federal Line 5b less only military, railroad and CT teachers' pay); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 32,000.00 + public pension (NY) 30,000.00 = 62,000.00. Federal taxable income = 62,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 46,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 62,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 62,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b pension and annuity (Line 5b part): federal AGI 62,000.00 is under the 75,000.00 test, decimal 1; 30,000.00 x 1 = 30,000.00 -> 30,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 30,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 30,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 62,000.00 - 30,000.00 = 32,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 32,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 32,000.00 is more than 31,000.00, exemption 13,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 32,000.00 - 13,000.00 = 19,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 19,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 9,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 405.00 = 605.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 32,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 605.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.13 (Connecticut AGI 32,000.00 is in the band more than 31,800.00); Line 9 = 605.00 x 0.13 = 78.65. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 605.00 - 78.65 = 526.35 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: A New York State pension is treated like any other pension on Line 48b: the booklet names no other-state rule and the worksheet takes all of Line 5b, so it is subtracted in full below the 75,000 test.
